summary: Reproduced the Model Gateway MCP tool_choice rewrite in both non-streaming and streaming Responses paths. The initial upstream request now preserves an explicit client choice, omitted choices still default to auto, and post-MCP resume requests explicitly use auto.

tests.what_was_measured: Captured two actual mock-upstream /v1/responses payloads; the initial payload was auto instead of the requested required value.
Captured the streaming mock-upstream request sequence; the initial payload was auto instead of required, while MCP execution and the final assistant message completed.
The non-streaming upstream request sequence was required then auto; the follow-up contained function_call_output and the response contained the completed MCP call and final assistant message.
The streaming upstream request sequence was required then auto; the follow-up contained function_call_output and the SSE response contained the completed MCP call and final assistant message.
Two boundary tests passed: explicit required/auto/none choices are preserved for initial requests, and an omitted choice defaults to auto.
Rust formatting and patch whitespace checks passed.

gpu_execution.evidence: The defect is deterministic JSON routing in the Rust Model Gateway and was reproduced with its in-process mock OpenAI worker and mock MCP server; no model computation or GPU kernel is involved.

remaining_limitations: No real model weights or external MCP service were used; the deterministic fixture validates Model Gateway transport, MCP execution, request sequencing, and response assembly only.
No GPU execution was performed because this routing-only defect does not enter SGLang model execution.
An upstream candidate fix exists at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31469 and was open when reviewed.
